details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has lowered its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.0% from its April projection of 3.1%. This adjustment is largely attributed to the ongoing Middle East conflict's impact on energy markets and global supply chains. However, the IMF noted that a booming investment in artificial intelligence is partially mitigating these negative effects. Global headline inflation is now expected to rise to 4.7% in 2026.
title: IMF Trims Global Growth to 3% Amid Geopolitical Shocks and Inflation

details: European Central Bank (ECB) policymaker Yannis Stournaras has stated that renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran have driven energy prices higher, effectively bringing the ECB back to "square one" in its battle against inflation within the Eurozone. Markets are now anticipating further interest rate hikes from the ECB to counter the escalating inflationary pressures.
title: ECB Warns of Renewed Inflation Risks Due to US-Iran Conflict

details: Bitcoin has recovered above the $60,000 mark following comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh regarding lower inflation risks, which sparked optimism in cryptocurrency markets. Despite this rebound, the crypto market continues to be highly sensitive to Federal Reserve communications, inflation data, and broader monetary policy, increasingly mirroring traditional risk assets.
title: Bitcoin Reclaims $60K Amid Fed Policy Shifts, Remains Macro-Sensitive

details: Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, has received formal approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to establish Circle National Trust, a national digital currency trust bank. This regulatory breakthrough is seen as a significant step, enhancing confidence in stablecoins and indicating a growing institutional integration for digital assets within the traditional financial system.
title: Stablecoin Issuer Circle Secures US Digital Currency Trust Bank License

details: A four-year prohibition on the issuance of a U.S. central bank digital currency (CBDC) is set to become law. This ban, embedded within a housing bill, will prevent the Federal Reserve from issuing a digital dollar through December 31, 2030, reflecting strong opposition from the crypto industry and Republican lawmakers concerned about government surveillance and centralization.
title: US Digital Dollar Ban to Become Law Until End of 2030
